title: Critical-path decomposition and floating surge pool for cycle-level capacity allocation
creator: Priya Shah
description: Create a repeatable decision flow and operational mechanism to: 1) decompose cycle-level initiatives into critical-path tickets, 2) maintain a small floating surge pool of engineers that can be redeployed mid-cycle, and 3) codify scope-cut heuristics for graceful downgrade. This ticket produces the playbook, staffing matrix, and a lightweight dashboard for planning conversations.
background: Repeated mid-cycle escalations in the last three cycles exposed two pain points: teams carrying too much non-critical scope and lack of a fast, low-friction way to move engineers between initiatives. Current reserve approaches (large static buffers or ad-hoc reassignments) either waste capacity or introduce operational churn. We need a predictable, low-latency mechanism to reallocate headcount and trim scope without derailing dependent work.
goals: Define an explicit critical-path decomposition template for PMs and Eng leads
Design a floating surge pool model (size, eligibility, on-call rotation for surge)
Produce a decision matrix for scope cuts and acceptable regressions
Ship a one-page dashboard to show capacity vs committed effort and surge availability
acceptance_criteria: A filled critical-path template used in planning for >= 3 initiatives in the cycle
Surge pool staffing model agreed by Eng and People and piloted with 6 engineers for one cycle
Scope-cut decision matrix accepted by Exec PM review and applied to 2 candidate initiatives
Dashboard (Grafana/Metabase link) showing committed points, surge pool, and at-risk tickets is live and referenced in weekly PM sync
out_of_scope: Full rework of sprint tooling or estimation system
Detailed cost modeling for Dedicated capacity — that remains an ENG/infra project
approach: Work in three parallel streams: (A) Template + training: build a two-page critical-path template (business outcome, must-have vs nice-to-have, strict dependencies, test/QA delta); (B) Surge pool ops: define eligibility, rotation cadence, swap window, and an on-call for surge handoff; (C) Visualization: implement a small dashboard showing committed effort by initiative, surge pool count, and ticket-level risk flags. Engagement: run two planning workshops with Eng leads and TPMs to iterate on the template and the matrix.
tradeoffs: Small surge pool reduces idle time but increases context-switching and ramp costs
Aggressive scope cuts preserve launch date but risk product quality regressions; matrix will aim to prefer deferring non-customer-visible polish
More prescriptive templates speed decisions but reduce local team autonomy; we'll pilot with opt-in teams first
risks: Teams may game the critical-path designation to preserve scope
People team capacity constraints could limit surge pool staffing
Dashboards may reflect stale data if ticket statuses aren't kept up to date
